reviewer_checks_pass: The packet check matched the exact candidate, spec SHA-256, and packet SHA-256.

Exporter body statement and block counts are computed from the complete MIR lists. StorageLive/StorageDead are exempted only from the unsupported-statement classifier; supported bodies are still encoded through the ordinary complete basic-block encoder, which serializes both event kinds. The new admission does not filter these statements or decrement counts.

Exporter remains limited to one block, Return terminator, bounded locals/statements, bare-local assignments, and the existing Copy/Move use or pointer-cast rvalues. Every other non-assignment statement still receives an unsupported reason; Nop, PlaceMention, and FakeRead now have explicit refusal labels.

Translator derives the unique set of storage-event locals from the full statement list, validates each against the declared locals, rejects argument/return markers and non-raw-pointer types, and then replays events in original order. The ordered trace records each storage event and cast with source/destination local ordinals and typed edge.

Explicitly marked locals begin unallocated in the checker state, require one Live before use and one Dead after receiving a projection value, and reject duplicate/repeated, unmatched, overlapping, or unbalanced events. Casts reject dead sources and destinations. The one-pair limit is conservative: Rust MIR permits more general lifecycle patterns, but unsupported repeated cycles are refused rather than normalized.

Locals with no storage markers are treated as live throughout, consistent with Rustc MIR documentation. The receiver is initially initialized; all other projection values must be established by the checked cast assignments and existing provenance checks.

The complete projection record, including the new ordered trace, is compared structurally between the actual standard callee descriptor and the same-unit checked helper descriptor. Signature, generic binding T=u64, one-block/Return shape, pointer types, cast kinds, linear dataflow, local count/mutability, body counts, helper source contract, and helper HIR lifetime restrictions remain enforced.

The existing caller checks still require the unique actual as_mut_ptr call and descriptor, exact Ref/Unsize/local/call source trace, exact source lifetime, reversible full_borrow resource sequence, original normal successor, and existing normal/unwind restoration. The P13 patch does not change runtime source, CFG, schema, refiner, kernel, or trusted assumptions.

The recorded Rustc MIR documentation says unmarked locals are implicitly allocated for the full function and documents the more permissive repeated StorageLive/StorageDead behavior. The implementation deliberately accepts only a single balanced pair, so that broader behavior is not imported into the proof checker: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/nightly-rustc/rustc_middle/mir/enum.StatementKind.html#variant.StorageLive.
